newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end little changed after Fed hike.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end little changed after Fed hike.

text.p: Canadian bonds gave up early gains to close little changed on Tuesday, weakening along with U.S. Treasuries following a widely expected hike in U.S. interest rates, analysts said.

"There is still a bit of a knee-jerk reaction here with the curve flattening in sympathy with the U.S. curve," said Anita Lauria, an economist with Salomon Brothers. "There's still a lack of conviction here and an uncertainty about how much tightening is ahead."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond closed up C$0.10 to C$109.35 to yield 7.199 percent.
Before the Fed announcement the bond had been trading up C$0.60 to C$109.85 to yield 7.159 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond ended down 14/32 to yield 6.96 percent following the rate rise. The spread between the two narrowed to 24 basis points from 29 basis points at the close of trading on Monday.

Analysts said there were several reasons for Canada's bond market outperformance. One of which was the fact that the Canadian dollar traded steady even though the Bank of Canada did not match the Fed rate increase. The Canadian dollar has traditionally weakened following Fed rate rises.
Canadian bond investors will now be closely monitoring the performance of the currency, analysts said. If the dollar remains firm the Bank of Canada is seen holding interest rates steady.

"I think everyone's got a very close eye on it (the currency), so I think it's going to dictate the direction over the near term," said Rich Wylie, a fixed-income economist with TD Securities Inc. "Right now it certainly looks like we've had this meeting come and go without too much of a negative impact in Canada."
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.25 to C$102.65 to yield 6.623. The U.S. bond fell 13/32 to yield 6.76 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 14 basis points from 12 basis points on Monday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.22 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.40 percent.
